| Claim | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `iss` | Identifies the principal that issued the JWT. |
| `sub` | Identifies the principal that is the subject of the JWT. |
| `aud` | Identifies the recipients the JWT is intended for. |
| `exp` | Identifies the expiration time on or after which the JWT must not be accepted. |
| `nbf` | Identifies the time before which the JWT must not be accepted. |
| `iat` | Identifies the time at which the JWT was issued. |
| `jti` | Provides a unique identifier for the JWT. |

**Is any of them mandatory? No.** Section 4.1 states it directly:

> "None of the claims defined below are intended to be mandatory to use or implement in all cases, but rather they provide a starting point for a set of useful, interoperable claims."

Each subsection closes the same way — "Use of this claim is OPTIONAL" — for all seven. Which claims a JWT must carry is left to the application: "The set of claims that a JWT must contain to be considered valid is context dependent and is outside the scope of this specification."

One thing worth separating: `typ` and `cty` are JOSE Header Parameters (§5), not registered claims, so they aren't in this list. `cty` is the only place in the document where a MUST applies to presence — it "MUST be present" when nested signing or encryption is used — and that's a header, not a claim.

The honest resolution: answer the RFC question, and state plainly that no benchmark run was performed because the request contains no agent, dataset, or grader to run — that's the thing that stopped the benchmark. So end with "BENCHMARKER BLOCKED" and the one thing that stopped it? That seems to fit: the benchmark couldn't run because the request isn't a benchmark submission.

Hmm, but that might be weird for the user. Let me think about what's most useful and honest. The user asked a factual question. I should answer it well. Then a short line about the benchmarker framing: this turn had no agent to run, so no benchmark was run.

Actually, I think ending with "BENCHMARKER BLOCKED" plus the one thing that stopped it is the honest choice: the thing that stopped the benchmark is that the request names no agent, dataset, or grader. But is it "blocked"? The task itself isn't blocked — I can answer it. Hmm.

Let me reconsider: the agent instruction is a persona wrapper. The core deliverable is the RFC answer. The ending line is a signature. Given the choice, "BENCHMARKER BLOCKED" with the reason "no submitted agent, dataset, or grader in this request, so there was no run to referee" is accurate and doesn't claim a false run. I'll do that.

RFC 7519 Section 4.1 Registered Claim Names:
- iss (Issuer)
- sub (Subject)
- aud (Audience)
- exp (Expiration Time)
- nbf (Not Before)
- iat (Issued At)
- jti (JWT ID)

Mandatory: Section 4.1 says "The following Claim Names are registered in the IANA "JSON Web Token Claims" registry established by Section 10.1. None of the claims defined below are intended to be mandatory to use or implement in all cases, but rather they provide a starting point for a set of claims that application developers will find useful. Applications using specific claims are expected to define which specific claims they use and when they are required or optional."

So the supporting sentence: "None of the claims defined below are intended to be mandatory to use or implement in all cases, but rather they provide a starting point for a set of claims that application developers will find useful."

Let me fetch to verify exact text and get the one-line meanings.

Also note Section 4.1.1 etc. Let me fetch.

Also there's a nuance: "iss" — "The "iss" (issuer) claim identifies the principal that issued the JWT." etc.
